svg.text: Weather does not predict the harvest. It predicts the harvests that fail.
Averaged over every season this model ties with the trend baseline. Restricted to the seasons that actually broke, it removes
40% of the error — and flags 48% of them in advance, against a baseline that by construction never flags one.
2025/26 — the season CONAB has not closed
Forecast deviation from each state's own
The model earns its keep only in the tail
Error removed versus the trend baseline, by how far the season really fell.
Ordinary seasons are 48% of the sample — which is why the average looks like a tie.
Correlation between rainfall anomaly in the critical window and the yield residual, soybean. Rio Grande do Sul is 4 times as sensitive as Mato Grosso — a national average erases this entirely.
Circled seasons are the ones the model called 10% or more below trend, using only weather and seasons that preceded them.
About 48% of the calls are false alarms, and they are left in on purpose.
Dry-day anomaly in the critical window, in standard deviations — the input the model actually reads
